dataset_family: Catholic Aging Brain Imaging (CABI) database: outpatients of the Catholic Brain Health Center, Yeouido St. Mary's Hospital, Catholic University of Korea, Seoul, 2017-2022; 126 amyloid-PET-positive MCI (66 DSM-5 MDD with HAMD-17 > 14, 60 without psychiatric disorder); retrospective, not public
method_family: Resting-state fMRI seed-to-voxel functional connectivity (PCC seed, CONN) group comparison plus FC-versus-HAMD-17 and FC-versus-amyloid SUVR correlations, and FreeSurfer cortical thickness group comparison, in 18F-flutemetamol-positive MCI; cross-sectional. Same broad method family as supporter P-643 (resting-state FC in amyloid-PET-characterised depressed MCI at a Korean memory clinic)
what_it_shows: Within amyloid-positive MCI, the MDD group had higher anterior-DMN connectivity (lateral temporal and medial prefrontal) than the no-depression group, and HAMD-17 total score correlated positively with medial-prefrontal anterior-DMN connectivity (FDR p < 0.05), while amyloid SUVR did not correlate with DMN connectivity. Cortical thickness did not differ between the depressed and non-depressed groups. All participants have MCI, so the first clause is not tested; there is no conversion outcome.
why: Wang et al., Brain Sci 2023;13:1111. The PDF title and authors match the summaries.md block and the map entry. As a SUPPORTER of the Table A1 row the paper fails: the supporter sentence says continuous severity scores fail to track brain measures, and P-549's own correlation shows depression severity (HAMD-17) tracking a functional brain measure (anterior-DMN FC). It would be brain-limb counter-evidence, opposite in result to P-643's null K-GDS-versus-FC correlations in a closely similar design. Caveats that make it WEAK counter-evidence on severity grading specifically: (1) the HAMD-17 distribution is bimodal by construction (no-depression 3.78 +/- 1.02; depression 16.52 +/- 2.53, since MDD required HAMD > 14), and the sample for the correlation is not stated, so if it is the pooled 126 the correlation largely re-expresses the MDD-versus-no-MDD group difference rather than grading within the depressed; (2) no correlation coefficient is printed, and Figure 3 is not in the extract; (3) the correlation was tested in the connectivity already defined by the group contrast, which risks circularity; (4) Table 1 prints 'NS' for HAM-D although the text says the depression group scored significantly higher, an internal inconsistency. None of these turns the result into a null, so the paper cannot be counted as support. The cortical-thickness null is a status contrast (MDD versus none) within amyloid-positive MCI, not a severity test, so it does not support the supporter sentence either. The 'although' clause (MDD lower FC than subthreshold) is not tested: the comparator here is no depression, and the direction found is HIGHER FC in MDD. Independence: CABI (Yeouido St. Mary's, Catholic University of Korea) is a different institution from P-643 (Korea University Guro), and no author is shared with P-643 (Hyung et al.), P-974 (Chosun) or P-989 (SMG-SNU Boramae). Not a preprint (peer-reviewed MDPI journal). Symbols in quotes are transliterated to ASCII (Abeta, +/-).

quotes.quote: A total of 126 Abeta-positive MCI patients were included, with 66 having depression and 60 without depression. The results revealed increased functional connectivity in the anterior DMN in the depression group compared to the non-depression group. The functional connectivity of the anterior DMN positively correlated with depression severity but not with Abeta deposition.

The no-depression group had no clinically significant psychiatric disorders (depressive disorder, schizophrenia, or bipolar disorder). The depression group had additional inclusion criteria as follows: diagnosis of major depressive disorder according to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM)-V criteria [30] with 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD17) total score > 14 [31].
The depression group had significantly higher HAMD17 total scores than the no-depression group (Table 1).

No significant correlations between the global mean SUVR scores and functional connectivity were observed. However, the HAMD17 total scores showed a positive correlation with the medial pre-frontal cortex of the anterior DMN functional connectivity (Figure 3, FDR corrected p < 0.05).
